what_it_does: Running large language models (AI chat systems) on graphics cards (GPUs) burns a lot of electricity, and the operators of these services must keep response times within promised limits. The problem is that the GPU's clock speed is usually set to maximum even when demand is light and the work could be done just as fast at lower speed. This paper introduces a system called throttLL'eM that uses a small machine-learning predictor to forecast, a few moments ahead, how much memory the model will need and how many requests are arriving, then adjusts the GPU's speed accordingly. By running the GPU slower when the predicted load is light, the system cuts energy use while still meeting the agreed response-time targets. The predictor is reported to be highly accurate, with mispredictions causing less than one extra step per second on average.
